chunks: I asked Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him) about a man who said 'Bismillah' and shot at a prey, but missed it and hit another. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He may eat from it.'

key_terms.أَخْطَأَ: Missed/erred; the shot deviated from the intended target
key_terms.سَمَّى: Pronounced the name of Allah (said 'Bismillah') — a required condition for the permissibility of slaughtered or hunted animals
key_terms.صَيْد: Game/prey; an animal hunted in the wild

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat an animal accidentally hit while hunting if Bismillah was said?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal question posed to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about the permissibility of eating game that was not the intended target of a hunt but was struck after the hunter had properly said 'Bismillah' (in the Name of Allah). The Imam ruled that the meat is permissible to eat. This ruling reflects the Islamic principle that the intention and the pronunciation of the name of Allah at the time of releasing the weapon are the key determining factors for lawfulness, and that accidental deviation of the weapon does not nullify the hunt's permissibility.
